extracted.intended_audience: students or readers of historical arithmetic/practical mathematics (Italian)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and worked methods for dividing profits, capital, goods, and recurring earnings among partners or claimants according to time, contribution, and proportion (historic Italian arithmetic manual style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Share profits proportional to capital × time
rubrics_metrics.description: When partners contribute different capitals for different durations, compute each partner's product of capital and time and divide the total profit in proportion to those products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply each partner's invested sum by the time it was invested (capital × months/years). Sum those products to get the proportional base; each partner's share = (their product / total products) × total gain. The page gives many numeric examples applying this rule to form the division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cross-multiplication (la regola multiplicando in croci) for proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve proportional (rule-of-three) problems by multiplying 'in croce' (cross-multiplying) and dividing to find the unknown term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form a proportion between known quantities and the unknown, multiply across (cross), then divide by the remaining known term. The text repeatedly instructs 'la regola multiplicando in croci' and demonstrates cross-multiplication to compute shares, rates, and equivalent values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert heterogeneous contributions to a common monetary value before dividing
rubrics_metrics.description: If contributions are in different items (animals, goods) or mixed assets, assign each item a monetary value and convert the whole capital to money before applying proportional division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include valuing a cow and a calf (vacca e vitello) and converting them to a monetary sum, then treating that sum as capital in the proportional division. The page instructs calculating the value of mixed goods and then dividing as with cash capitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportion indivisible units and remainders by proportional rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: When dividing totals that contain indivisible small units (coins, indivisible items), compute proportional fractional shares, allocate the integer parts, and distribute the remainder according to the proportion or stipulated rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual shows many numeric divisions where remainders occur; guidance is to determine each partner's proportional share, take the integral part for each, and then handle the leftover units (rounding rules and small adjustments appear in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce different payment/earning periods to a common time basis
rubrics_metrics.description: When earnings or payments accrue with different periodicities or at different times, convert all amounts to a common time unit (months, years) before computing proportional shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives cases with partners entering/leaving at different months and instructs computing capital×time using the same time unit for all partners, then dividing profit per the products. It includes worked examples of converting multi-year/multi-month schedules to the common basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recompute shares on dissolution or change of contributions using accrued capital-time
rubrics_metrics.description: When a partnership is dissolved or partner contributions change mid-period, determine each partner's accrued capital×time up to dissolution/change and divide gains accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show partners who change the amounts they 'metta' or who join/leave; the rule is to account for each partner's actual invested sum and the time it remained invested up to the reckoning point, then recompute products and divide the total gain on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportion periodic rents/earnings proportionally to capital or share-holders
rubrics_metrics.description: For recurring annual incomes or rents tied to capital, treat each year's income proportionally to the capital basis and apportion to partners accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contains examples where annual / periodic gains are tied to capitals and instructs treating yearly gains as proportional to capitals (and time) — e.g., compute annual gain per unit capital and multiply by each partner's capital share across the relevant years.
